title: Leonardo da Vinci designs a mechanical knight
description: Leonardo sketches a cable-and-pulley automaton in the shape of an armoured knight, able to sit, move its arms, turn its head and open its jaw.
why_it_mattered: The earliest known European engineering design for a programmable humanoid — the idea of building an artificial human as a machine problem, centuries before the means existed.

title: Gakutensoku, the first robot built in Asia
description: Biologist Makoto Nishimura completes Gakutensoku in Osaka: a large pneumatic figure that changes expression and moves its head and arms, built for imperial enthronement celebrations.
why_it_mattered: Marked non-Western entry into humanoid building and, unusually for the period, framed the robot as a friendly study of nature rather than a mechanical labourer.

title: Elektro walks and talks at the New York World's Fair
description: Westinghouse presents Elektro, a 2-metre motor-driven humanoid that walks on rollered feet, moves its arms and speaks 700 words from records, to huge fairground crowds.
why_it_mattered: Fixed the popular image of 'a robot' as a walking metal man and showed a corporation using a humanoid purely as public spectacle.

title: WABOT-1, the first full-scale anthropomorphic robot
description: Waseda University completes WABOT-1, which walks quasi-statically, grips objects with tactile hands, gauges distances by sight and holds a spoken Japanese conversation.
why_it_mattered: The first machine to integrate locomotion, manipulation, vision and speech in a human-scale body — the template every later humanoid follows.

title: Honda reveals P2, the first self-contained bipedal humanoid
description: After a decade of secret work, Honda unveils P2: a humanoid carrying its own battery, computer and radio link that walks, climbs stairs and pushes carts using predictive control.
why_it_mattered: Proved an untethered humanoid could balance and walk dynamically in the real world, and kicked off the modern corporate humanoid race.

title: ASIMO's public debut
description: Honda introduces ASIMO, a 130 cm humanoid that goes on to tour the world, ring the NYSE bell, conduct an orchestra and appear in classrooms and ads for nearly two decades.
why_it_mattered: For a generation ASIMO simply was 'the humanoid robot', setting public expectations for what the machines could and could not do.

title: Robonaut 2 is launched to the International Space Station
description: NASA's dexterous humanoid torso R2 flies to the ISS aboard Space Shuttle Discovery and is installed inside the station, the first humanoid robot in space.
why_it_mattered: Put a human-shaped robot into an operational off-world workplace, and framed shared human/robot tools and workspaces as a design goal.

title: SCHAFT wins the DARPA Robotics Challenge trials
description: SCHAFT's electrically actuated S-One posts the top score at the 2013 DRC trials; Google acquires the company within days and later withdraws it from the finals.
why_it_mattered: Showed high-power electric actuation could rival hydraulics for heavy tasks, and marked big tech's first serious move into humanoids.

title: Sophia is granted honorary Saudi 'citizenship'
description: At a Riyadh investment conference, Hanson Robotics' Sophia is announced as a citizen of Saudi Arabia — a publicity move widely covered and widely criticised.
why_it_mattered: Became the reference point for debate about humanoid hype, anthropomorphism and premature talk of 'robot rights'.

title: QRIO becomes the first humanoid to run
description: Sony demonstrates its knee-high QRIO briefly leaving the ground with both feet during a running gait, along with push recovery and coordinated group dancing.
why_it_mattered: Pushed bipedal control past the static-stability comfort zone into true dynamic, flight-phase motion.

title: NAO becomes the RoboCup Standard Platform
description: RoboCup's Standard Platform League adopts Aldebaran's NAO as the single common robot all teams must use, replacing the Sony AIBO.
why_it_mattered: Gave thousands of students and researchers the same affordable humanoid, making NAO the most widely used humanoid platform in education and research.

title: iCub is released as an open-source humanoid
description: IIT publishes the full hardware and software design of its child-sized iCub under free licences; dozens of labs build or acquire one.
why_it_mattered: Created a shared, modifiable research humanoid, so manipulation and embodied-cognition results could be reproduced across institutions.

title: DARPA Robotics Challenge finals
description: Humanoid and humanoid-like robots attempt a course of driving, walking on rubble, opening doors, cutting a hole and turning valves; KAIST's DRC-HUBO+ wins. Many robots fall on live TV.
why_it_mattered: The most rigorous public test of whole-body humanoid capability to date, and an honest, widely seen measure of how far real-world reliability still had to go.

title: Tesla announces the Optimus humanoid
description: At its AI Day, Tesla says it will build a general-purpose humanoid using its car-derived AI and hardware, targeting mass production and a low price.
why_it_mattered: Reframed humanoids from research curiosity to mass-market product ambition and pulled a wave of funding and new companies into the field.

title: Agility opens RoboFab, the first humanoid factory
description: Agility Robotics opens a Salem, Oregon plant designed to build Digit at a rate of thousands per year.
why_it_mattered: Marked the shift from hand-built prototypes to volume manufacturing as the industry's stated goal.

title: Boston Dynamics retires hydraulic Atlas and unveils an electric one
description: One day after posting a farewell montage for the hydraulic Atlas, Boston Dynamics reveals an all-electric Atlas with continuously rotating joints, aimed at Hyundai factory work.
why_it_mattered: The field's most famous hydraulic humanoid going fully electric confirmed electric actuation as the settled choice for general-purpose humanoids.

title: Unitree G1 breaks the US$20k price barrier
description: Unitree begins selling the compact G1 humanoid from around US$16,000, far below competitors priced in the six figures.
why_it_mattered: Put a capable humanoid within reach of ordinary university budgets, and G1 quickly became a default research and benchmarking platform.

title: Figure puts a vision-language-action model on-board with Helix
description: Figure AI ends its OpenAI partnership and shows Helix, an in-house model that maps camera images and spoken instructions directly to whole-body robot actions on Figure 02.
why_it_mattered: A visible marker of the shift from scripted humanoid demos to learned, language-conditioned control as the industry's main bet for autonomy.

title: China open-sources a full-size electric humanoid
description: The Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center releases the running humanoid Tiangong as open source; Fourier's open N1 and UC Berkeley's sub-$5k Humanoid Lite follow within months.
why_it_mattered: Started an open-hardware track for humanoids, lowering the barrier to entry the way open designs earlier did for drones and 3D printers.

sources.title: Tiangong goes open source — Interesting Engineering

title: Beijing stages the first humanoid half-marathon
description: Around twenty teams race humanoid robots over a 21 km course beside human runners in Beijing's E-Town; a Tiangong robot finishes first in roughly two hours forty minutes, with most entrants needing battery swaps or human support.
why_it_mattered: A public endurance benchmark — and a candid demonstration that reliability and stamina, not peak agility, are the current limits.

sources.title: Tiangong upgraded as humanoid robot prepares for race day — Mike Kalil

title: Humanoids enter automotive plants for paid pilots
description: Within roughly a year, Figure runs 02 at BMW Spartanburg, Apptronik pilots Apollo with Mercedes-Benz, and UBTECH trials Walker S at BYD, Nio and a Foxconn plant.
why_it_mattered: Moved general-purpose humanoids from staged demos to recurring shifts on real production lines — the first at-scale test of whether the economics work.
